passages.provision_quote: 9. Subject to subsection F of this section, for taxable years beginning from and after December 31 of the year in which notice is provided to the department pursuant to section 43-243, subsection B, paragraph 2, the tax is 2.5% of taxable income.
passages.note: SB 1828 (2021) is a multi-subject omnibus that amends unemployment insurance benefits (Title 23), property tax valuation ratios, sales tax exemptions, tax credits, fire district taxes, and income tax rates, including a flat 2.5% rate.
Bill overview lists Mesnard as Prime sponsor of SB 1828 (2021), the omnibus taxation bill.
Senate Third Reading on SB 1828 (2021) passed 16-14 with Mesnard voting Yea.

rows.reasoning: SB 1828 (2021), on which Mesnard was Prime sponsor and voted Yea on final passage (16-14), is an omnibus bill (short title 'omnibus; taxation') that bundles unrelated subjects: unemployment-insurance wage base and benefits (Title 23), property-tax valuation ratios, sales-tax exemptions, several tax credits, fire-district tax caps, and the income-tax rate cut to a flat 2.5%. Per the taxes annex's Omnibus rule, a sponsor or voter on such a bill is not shown to support any one tax clause (e.g., the rate cut in Sec. 43-1011, matching rung 4's 'cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay') absent his own words tying the act to that provision, which none of the sources here supply.
needs_source: Mesnard's own statement or floor speech tying his SB 1828 vote or sponsorship specifically to the income-tax-rate-cut provision (Sec. 43-1011), since the bill also enacts unrelated unemployment-insurance, property-tax, and sales-tax provisions.
A single-subject income-tax-rate bill sponsored or voted on by Mesnard, if one exists, to establish a chair without relying on the SB 1828 omnibus.
